$comment: Operations of the API that no SDK's hand-written layer models, and why. `scripts/sdk-contract/build.py --check` fails on an operation that is neither claimed by a manifest nor matched here, and on an entry here that matches nothing the API still serves. So this file is the record of a decision, not a place to make a failure go away: a new endpoint stops CI until somebody either wires it into a client or writes one line about why no client needs it. Patterns are fnmatch globs over `METHOD /path`, with the path exactly as the OpenAPI document templates it.

omit.reason: The operator console's own surface. It is behind require_admin and has one client, the console; no SDK models it (ADR 0013).

Account bootstrap and key minting. An SDK is constructed with a key it already holds; the flows that produce one belong to the console and to `fountain auth login` (#1305). Only GET /api/auth/me is modelled, because a client wants to know whose key it has.

Claimable principals (ADR 0044). A trusted application opens and claims these with its own full-scope key; the credential that comes back is an ordinary API key, so an SDK's job starts after this point and every endpoint it already models is what the principal then uses. Paddock is the first caller and reaches these four over plain HTTP.
Sign in with Fountain. The browser apps run the code+PKCE dance themselves against these two, and the token they get IS an API key, so the SDK starts after this point.
Account self-service: billing, credit checkout, data exports, inference credentials, onboarding. The console owns all of it and none of it is part of running an agent.
Webhook registration and delivery replay. Server-to-server configuration a person does once in the console; nothing an SDK caller does per run.
Egress broker bindings (ADR 0019). Configuration of where a credential lives, set once per account; the run-time effect is invisible to a client.
Self-hosted runner registration and the daemon's WebSocket (ADR 0022). The `fountain runner` daemon is the only client, and its socket is not JSON over HTTP.
The Buzz gateway's own provisioning surface (ADR 0020). Buzz calls it; no general client does.
Bulk upsert of a compiled fountain.yml. The CLI compiles the manifest and calls this; an SDK caller creates the resources it wants directly.
The AG-UI event stream. A second wire dialect for the same turn, consumed by AG-UI clients that already have their own protocol library; the SDKs follow /events and /stream instead.
The OpenAI-compatible gateway. Its clients are OpenAI SDKs by definition — that is the whole point of the shape.
Read-only console surfaces: the tenant's audit trail and the support inbox. No agent run touches them.
Avatar upload and generation. Image bytes for the console's own presentation, not part of any client's wire.
Agent version history, a console read. A conversation pins its version server-side, so a client never selects one.

Console-facing reads and the rented teammate contact (ADR 0030 decision 4). Each needs a UI around it — a connect button, an egress panel, an image, a phone number a person pays for — rather than a verb on a client.
kubelet's probes. Unauthenticated, and about the deployment rather than the API.
PUT aliases of the PATCH routes, kept for clients that only speak PUT. The SDKs model the PATCH, and the two share a controller action.
